clue.text: Warn upper-class type about parking next to one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the upper-class type goes round the other letters

parts.note: a toff is a posh, upper-class person

indicators.note: next to sets the parking letter directly beside the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A cautionary note about a posh driver who leaves the car beside a lone spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a quiet advance warning is the phrasal verb meaning to alert or forewarn them.

clue.text: Leading score is excellent

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
a notch is a score or cut mark, as on a tally stick

explanation.surface: A team in front on points is doing brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like points, but it is a scratch mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Dog shower?

definitions.meaning: a gundog breed that freezes to indicate game
one who shows, an indicator, read as show-er rather than a rain shower

explanation.surface: Is that a dog shower, for washing pets?
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hunting dog breed, and also a needle or arrow that indicates something.

clue.text: Influence in favour of church

parts.note: for means supporting or in favour of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Supporting the church gives you sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Power to affect or compel is a synonym for sway or influence.

clue.text: Exceptionally powerful man: the man controls boxing clubs

parts.note: the man gives the pronoun he

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for controls holds the clubs letter

parts.note: rules means governs or controls
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A strongman who also runs the local boxing clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' is the container signal, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of the twelve labours is the byword for a man of immense strength.

clue.text: Statues here in sand — earliest, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Statues set in the sand, perhaps the very first ones.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific island is famous for its giant moai, stone figures of heads and torsos.

clue.text: Girl jazz fan at home, in her element initially

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: in places the at-home word inside the following letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of element

parts.note: in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: A girl who loves jazz is at home and in her element.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name.

clue.text: Dog taken from pitch, about to be brought over

parts.note: to pitch is to lurch or roll, as a ship does

indicators.note: brought over means turned around, so the two-letter word is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dog is taken off a sports field, to be fetched back later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a playing field but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbreed hunting dog, often part greyhound, used by poachers.

clue.text: Visit's about aggressive mongrel in stable

indicators.note: about means around, so the visit word surrounds the dog

parts.note: to see a doctor is to visit them
a cur is a snappy, worthless dog

explanation.surface: A visit to a stable about a snarling dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a building for horses but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly fixed and not likely to give way means steady or stable.

clue.text: It dropped from highest place in monastery

indicators.note: dropped from says the word It is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: priority is first or top place in an order of importance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something fell from the top of a monastery's tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IT from PRIORITY leaves the religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious house governed by a prior or prioress is a small kind of monastery.

clue.text: English boozer used by man full of mystery

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: An English drinker exploited by some mysterious man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' looks like a British pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arcane, understood only by a select few initiates, seems mysterious to everyone else.

clue.text: By no means love performing

parts.note: love is nothing, the zero score in tennis
doing means performing

explanation.surface: Absolutely not willing to perform for love.
explanation.definitionFit: This colloquial phrase is a firm refusal, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Honest one managed to win

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters have been handled and arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: One honest competitor somehow pulled off a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honest' looks like the definition, but it is anagram material with 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet placed this way at the racecourse pays only if the horse finishes first, not merely placed.

clue.text: Number in Somerset he rang?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Was it a phone number in Somerset that he dialled?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure but means something that numbs. Somerset is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was an early general anaesthetic, a thing that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Special choir arrives in the coastal area surrounding Falmouth

indicators.note: special suggests these letters are being put into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A noted choir comes to sing on the Cornish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Falmouth is a port town in Cornwall, England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the holiday nickname for the south Cornish coastline, where the port of Falmouth lies.

clue.text: A powder: one in tumbler son swallowed?

indicators.note: swallowed means the son letter is taken inside the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: A powder, a single dose in a glass that the son gulped down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in tumbler' reads as one item in a glass, which is how the letters line up once the son is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish-derived gelatin, used for clarifying beer and wine, is often sold dried as a powder.

clue.text: Mean to consume mostly raw fish

indicators.note: to consume means to take inside, so the mean word holds the rest

parts.note: stingy means mean with money

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A miser eats most of a raw fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Playing valet, Valentino in film

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rudolph Valentino takes the role of a valet in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1944 Elizabeth Taylor horse-racing picture is a famous Hollywood movie.

clue.text: Fat duke and I entertained by a model

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A plump duke and I are hosted by a model.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means fatty or relating to body fat, as in fatty tissue.

clue.text: Most conceited, leading character wearing crop top outside?

indicators.note: outside means the garment goes round the other letters

parts.note: a crop top is a short sleeveless vest
A is the first letter of the alphabet
in means wearing, as in a person in a hat

explanation.surface: The vainest star of the show, sporting a crop top?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' sounds like a film star but is the first letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of vain, meaning the most proud of one's own looks or abilities.

clue.text: You're on a Greek river that's rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Accepting a bet on a swelling Greek river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You're on!' is how one accepts a bet or challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'You're on' is an idiom that accepts a challenge, signalling consent.

clue.text: One wearing medal is leaving

indicators.note: wearing means the medal is put on, so it surrounds the one

parts.note: gong is informal British slang for a medal or decoration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A decorated veteran is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: GONG is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone departing a place is said to be on their way out, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Ground in lane with odd weed

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A strange weed growing in the ground of a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil, but it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant with a fluffy seed head is a common garden pest.

clue.text: Delete some letters stored in computer as evidence

indicators.note: some letters stored in says the answer is a few consecutive letters within the words

explanation.surface: Wipe the files kept on a computer as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or remove completely, the plain synonym for delete.

clue.text: English turn on chap at one area showing obsessive self-interest

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a man is a chap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Englishman turns on a fellow, all about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an extreme, fixated preoccupation with oneself and one's own importance.

clue.text: Rush job

definitions.meaning: to hurtle along fast and out of control

explanation.surface: A frantic push to get a task done.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to dash headlong; as a noun, one's working life or profession.

clue.text: Groom ahead of time in equestrian event

indicators.note: ahead of puts the groom word before the time word

parts.note: to dress hair or a horse is to groom it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A stable hand arrives early for a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like a stable worker, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Olympic horse-riding discipline in which the horse performs precise trained movements.

clue.text: Guard's second appearance

parts.note: an entry is a coming in, an appearance on stage

explanation.surface: A guard turns up for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted on watch at a gate or post is a guard.
